usual_baseline: Screening with the 4AT or CAM is usually poor: 0–34% in most wards, as low as 2.7% [1829] and 3% [1870]. Delirium is common (14.5–50.7%) but rarely named in the notes (8.5–19%). Care plans and PINCH-ME risk factor work are documented in 8.5–28%. Antipsychotics are started without a diagnosis [1893].
fix_that_works: Changes built into the notes work best. Electronic notes with a compulsory screen and switch to 4AT: 3% to 87% [1870]. A champions group plus proforma with 4AT sticker: 0% to 92% [1813]. A co-designed admission proforma: 53% to 79% [1899]. Bedside CAM-ICU training cut misdiagnosed 'psychosis' from 63% to 31% [1365].
fix_that_fails: Education, stickers and reminder emails: 4AT hit 100% in week 3 then fell to 1.3% by week 6 [1804]. Teaching alone: 25% to 35% [1153]. Lanyard cards: 9.5% to 43% [1898]; 7.5% to 40.6% [3466]. A bedside tool: 34% to 44% [1917]. Gains fell back between PDSA cycles [1846]. Formal diagnosis and management stayed low.
consultant_advice: Heavily overdone, with 17 audits and the same poor screening rate. Don't repeat a screening count. Only a compulsory electronic field or a proforma held gains. More useful: whether a positive 4AT leads to a diagnosis and a PINCH-ME plan, and antipsychotic use without a diagnosis.
